Studied: Investigation.name: Studied: Investigation
Studied: Investigation.description:
🔍 You studied how to work out what happened: criminology classes, a newspaper club, a detective agency job or years of case files.

🌱 You read a scene and its evidence, build timelines, interview witnesses, check alibis and notice what does not fit.
⚠️ Forensic labs, Quirk-based crimes and professional cover-ups outpace you, and you can commit to a wrong theory.
⚖️ You are not police: no searches, no seizing evidence, no entering a sealed scene, and tampering with one is a crime.
🏫 It shows in notes, pointed questions and a refusal to accept the first explanation.

📈 Grants: Investigation +15
Studied: Investigation.traitNarrativeEffects: The character has studied investigation: reading a scene and its evidence, building timelines, interviewing witnesses, checking alibis and tracing records. They notice what does not fit and write it down. Prior study, not mastery: forensic labs, Quirk-based crimes and professional cover-ups still outpace them, and they can commit to a wrong theory. Not a license: they are not police; they cannot search, seize evidence, question suspects with authority or enter a sealed scene, and tampering with one is a crime. It shows in notes, pointed questions and a refusal to accept the first explanation.
